title: Azerbaijan launches an offensive in Nagorno-Karabakh described as an anti-terrorist operation
body:
On Tuesday, 19 September 2023 Azerbaijan announced what it called anti-terrorist operations in Nagorno-Karabakh and demanded the complete withdrawal of ethnic Armenian forces. State news agency reports, citing the presidential administration, said operations would continue until Armenian units surrendered, handed over their weapons and dissolved what it called the illegal regime. Hikmet Hajiyev, foreign policy adviser to President Ilham Aliyev, told Reuters that Azerbaijani forces had broken through the line of contact in several places, and told Al Jazeera that the measures were local but limited. Armenia denied having forces in the area.

Nagorno-Karabakh's human rights ombudsman, Gegham Stepanyan, told Reuters that 25 people had been killed and 138 wounded, including 29 civilians, a figure Al Jazeera could not verify. He also said more than 7,000 people had been evacuated from 16 civilian communities. The separatist leadership proposed a ceasefire and talks with Baku that afternoon.

Armenia's foreign ministry urged Russian peacekeepers to intervene. France called for an emergency UN Security Council meeting, German Foreign Minister Annalena Baerbock said Azerbaijan had broken its promise, and the Kremlin said it was in contact with both sides. Turkey's foreign ministry said Azerbaijan had been forced to act. In Yerevan, hundreds of protesters gathered in Republic Square calling on Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan to resign.
